parts.title: Three young musicians
parts.stimulusHtml:
Ben

Ben started playing the guitar when he was eight. His uncle gave him an old guitar for his birthday and showed him a few songs. Now Ben plays in a band with two friends from school. They practise in Ben's garage every Friday evening, and his neighbours sometimes complain about the noise.

Carla

Carla plays the piano. She has lessons twice a week with a teacher who lives in the same street. Carla finds it difficult to play in front of other people, so she only plays at home. One day she would like to write music for films.

Dan

Dan learned to play the drums from videos on the internet. He practises for an hour every day after school. Last summer he won a music competition in his town, and the prize was a weekend at a music camp, where he met lots of other young drummers.

groups.instructions: For each question, choose the correct answer.

parts.title: My year at a school in the mountains
parts.stimulusHtml:
by Lucy Grant, aged 14

Last year my family moved to a small village in the mountains because my mum got a new job at the hospital there. I was worried at first, because my new school only had eighty students and I didn't know anyone.

On my first day, a girl called Rosa showed me around. She told me that in winter the students go skiing every Wednesday afternoon instead of having sports lessons. I had never skied before, and the first time I fell over about twenty times! By the end of the winter, though, I could ski down the hill behind the school without falling.

The thing I liked most was that the teachers knew every student's name. In my old school there were so many students that some teachers never remembered mine. The worst thing was the bus journey: it took fifty minutes each way, and the bus was often late when it snowed.

Now we have moved back to the city, but Rosa and I still talk online every weekend, and next February I am going to visit her for a week.
